northStar: A polished editorial scrollytelling experience about real operational friction. It must feel designed, not templated, and never like a SaaS carousel.
hardConstraints: The hero must immediately feel like a crowded real work desk: mail, Excel, Word, paper, calls, photos, attachments, notes.
On hero scroll, objects are attracted toward the centre while the scene fades into the next chapter; this is not an order/cleanup animation.

Desktop cases use one pinned stage controlled continuously by vertical scroll. Scenes transition with coordinated fade, x movement, depth and blur. Never expose a carousel track, arrows or cards sliding side by side.
Mobile cases are vertical and natural; no horizontal pinning.
Work objects must look recognisably like their real counterparts, not rectangles with labels.
White is dominant. #A0CDD2 is the only Stealth accent. No green. No AI gradients. No dark SaaS palette except the final CTA.
Use Manrope. No eyebrow marketing labels. No card grids. No giant bordered section containers.
Stealth enters only after the problem scenes, in the full-width blue pivot.
AI is one capability inside a real process, never the visual identity.
All motion is reversible and scroll-linked; no scroll-jacking.
prefers-reduced-motion and no-JS readability are mandatory.
Production content is editable through content.json without touching layout code.

motion.desktop: sticky scroll-linked scenes; continuous reversible interpolation
motion.mobile: natural vertical document flow; no horizontal stage
motion.references: Kortix-like rhythm and refinement without copying assets or identity

acceptance: hero reads as real operational chaos in under 2 seconds
horizontal chapter does not look like a carousel
active case is dominant while transitions stay elegant
blue pivot feels like narrative turn not decoration
